text:
Predicates:
Nice(x) ::: x is nice to animals.
Mean(x) ::: x is mean to animals.
Grumpy(x) ::: x is grumpy.
AnimalLover(x) ::: x is an animal lover.
PetOwner(x) ::: x is a pet owner.
LovesAnimals(x) ::: x loves animals.
Tom ::: a specific individual named Tom.
Premises:
¬(Nice(x) ∧ Mean(x)) ::: No one who is nice to animals is also mean to animals.
∃x (Grumpy(x) ∧ Mean(x)) ::: Some grumpy people are mean to animals.
∀x (AnimalLover(x) → Nice(x)) ::: All animal lovers are nice to animals.
∀x (PetOwner(x) → LovesAnimals(x)) ::: All pet owners love animals.
PetOwner(Tom) ::: Tom is a pet owner.
Conclusion:
¬(Grumpy(Tom) ∧ Mean(Tom)) ::: Tom is not both a grumpy person and mean to animals.
